author: show-me state times
title: Second pedestrian dies after Springfield vehicle crash on May 21
text:
William Turner, 28, of Springfield, died from injuries sustained in a vehicle crash that occurred on May 21, according to a May 27 announcement by the Springfield Police Department. Turner was the second pedestrian involved in the incident to die as a result of the crash.
The incident marks Springfield’s seventh fatal motor vehicle crash in 2026 and has resulted in eight deaths this year. The police previously reported that officers responded at 9:52 p.m. on May 21 to a collision involving pedestrians at Chestnut Expressway and Grant Avenue.
According to authorities, a 17-year-old driving a 2018 Dodge Charger eastbound struck two pedestrians who were crossing the road. Both individuals were transported to the hospital in critical condition. Christian Berry, age 32 and also from Springfield, later died from his injuries, while Turner remained hospitalized until his death was announced on May 25.
Police say the circumstances surrounding the crash remain under investigation. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the Springfield Police Department or submit an anonymous tip through Crime Stoppers online or by phone.
Springfield serves as the county seat of Greene County in southwestern Missouri and operates under a council-manager form of government adopted in 1953, with a nine-member City Council responsible for setting policy and direction, according to the official website.
